html:
Gandhara was an ancient kingdom and region in what is now northwest Pakistan and eastern Afghanistan, centred on the Peshawar valley. The map shows it around 500 BCE.

It was one of the Mahajanapadas, the great states of early India, with its chief cities at Taxila and Pushkalavati. In the late 500s BCE it became a province of the Achaemenid Empire of Persia. The grammarian Pāṇini probably came from here, and Taxila grew into a famous place of learning.

Gandhara sat on the road between Central Asia and India, so armies kept crossing it. Alexander came in 327 BCE. The Maurya, Indo-Greeks, Indo-Scythians and Parthians ruled in turn. Under the Kushan Empire, with its winter capital at Purushapura, Gandhara became a great Buddhist centre, and its sculptors mixed Greek and Indian styles in Greco-Buddhist art, making some of the first images of the Buddha.

The last kings of the region, the Hindu Shahis, were defeated near Peshawar by Mahmud of Ghazni in 1001.
sum: Gandhara was an ancient kingdom and region in what is now northwest Pakistan and eastern Afghanistan, centred on the Peshawar valley. The map shows it around 500 BCE.
